findings.patternName: Requested-vs-Received Principal Skew on Strategy Exit
findings.function: claim() L484 (skimSurplus return is authoritative) vs _getYieldForStrategy() L552-564 (totalBalanceOf-principalOf snapshot)
findings.description: Strong signature match. claim() prices the payment off the ACTUAL value returned by skimSurplus(token, claimer) (post-redeem/post-swap underlyingReceived, L484-489), while every preview/estimate path (calculateClaimAmount L675, getYield L731, getTotalYield L745) sums a SNAPSHOT surplus = totalBalanceOf - principalOf across getAuthorizedClients() in _getYieldForStrategy (L556-562). The two can diverge (large for AMM-routed strategies per the vault CLAUDE.md). In-scope manifestations: (1) preview-vs-actual divergence => the payment claim() charges can differ from calculateClaimAmount's quote, the front-run/MEV + overpay surface (profile PARK-06); (2) _getYieldForStrategy does NOT dedup clients[] before summing surplus (L556) — if getAuthorizedClients returns duplicates the ESTIMATE double-counts (the DB 'skim double-counts duplicate entries in clients[]' sub-condition). The principal-DECREMENT root cause itself lives in the OOS strategy adapter, so the deepest exploitability is cross-contract.
vulnerableWhenMatched: surplus skim relationship to principal can diverge from snapshot
clients[] not deduped before summing in the estimate
missingMitigations: no on-chain reconciliation of skimSurplus return against the snapshot estimate
presentMitigations: minRewardTokenSupplied floor in claim() (L501) lets the claimer bound delivered-yield-proxy downward
claim() pays strictly off the actual skimSurplus return, so SYA itself never under-backs principal
findings.routeTo: code-scanner + econ-scanner (cross-contract strategy-trust + MEV); root cause partly OOS
findings.note: Map to potential-high per DB severity, but the in-scope slice is the preview/estimate divergence + clients dedup, NOT a direct principal-skew in SYA (that accounting is in the strategy). Do not over-escalate without the strategy interaction context.

findings.function: claim() L497-498 (discount then denormalize); _denormalizeAmount L617-640; _normalizeAmount L586-609
findings.description: The literal divide-before-multiply ordering is NOT present (every step is mul-before-div: L497 multiplies by (10000-rate) before /10000; _normalizeAmount L598/L605 and _denormalizeAmount L629/L634 keep mul before div). The MATCH is to the precision/flooring family the pattern represents: claim() chains discount division (L497, /10000) then _denormalizeAmount down-scales by /(10**(18-decimals)) (L634). For a low-decimal rewardToken (e.g. 6-dec USDC) the compounded floor can drive actualPayment to 0 while real yield was already delivered by the skim loop — ledger L-01 zero-payment surface (profile PARK-02). minRewardTokenSupplied defaults to caller-chosen, and 0 disables the guard, so a careless/bot claimer can receive yield for ~0 payment. DECIMAL-ROUNDTRIP invariant: denormalize(normalize(x,t),t) <= x (floor), residual <1 ulp per token.
vulnerableWhenMatched: multi-step flooring (discount + decimal down-scale) can round actualPayment to 0
minRewardTokenSupplied=0 disables the only floor guard
missingMitigations: no explicit non-zero-payment floor / round-up on the protocol-favoring side
no minimum-yield enforcement independent of caller-supplied min
presentMitigations: mul-before-div ordering throughout (no classic precision-loss bug)
nudge split derived by subtraction (L512-513) so split has no extra drift
findings.note: DB severity MEDIUM. Ledger currently has the zero-payment as L-01 (Low). Re-surfaced for re-weigh: with a low-decimal rewardToken and discount, the floor-to-zero leak is a recurring value bleed, not a one-off. Confirm L-01 still live at this commit.

findings.function: claim() outer L464 + inner-exempt L473 + exempt-validate L453; _getYieldForStrategy clients L556; canClaim L706; getTotalYield L740; calculateClaimAmount L659/L667
findings.description: Multiple loops. Distinguishing the externally-growable ones from owner-bounded ones: (a) yieldStrategies[] loop in claim/calculateClaimAmount/getTotalYield/removeYieldStrategy is OWNER-bounded (addYieldStrategy is onlyOwner) — adding too many strategies until claim() exceeds the block gas limit and bricks the permissionless claim path is an owner FOOTGUN (Law 3 operational hazard), not a permissionless DoS. (b) the inner exemptStrategies[] loop (L473) is caller-supplied with NO length bound and NO dedup => O(nStrategies * nExempt), but the gas is borne by the caller's own tx (self-grief, not a DoS on others). (c) _getYieldForStrategy loops clients[] = strategy.getAuthorizedClients() (L556) — STRATEGY-controlled and externally growable; it sits inside calculateClaimAmount/getTotalYield/getYield previews, so an oversized client set can make the PREVIEW revert on gas, denying claimers the quote they use to set minRewardTokenSupplied. (d) canClaim loops 1..nftMinter.nextIndex() (L706) — NFTMinter-controlled, externally growable, but it is a view bot-helper never on the claim path. claim() itself does NOT loop clients (it calls skimSurplus once per strategy; the per-client work happens inside the OOS strategy and that gas is the claimer's).
vulnerableWhenMatched: clients[] (strategy-controlled) grows unbounded inside preview/view functions
missingMitigations: no length cap / dedup on exemptStrategies
no pagination on the preview helpers
presentMitigations: exemptStrategies escape hatch (M-04) lets a claimer skip a strategy whose skimSurplus runs out of gas
findings.routeTo: code-scanner (confirm preview-revert -> claim-quote denial chain); owner-footgun angle to severity-classifier
findings.note: DB severity MEDIUM. The reportable surfaces are the externally-growable clients[]/nextIndex view loops and the strategy-count owner footgun; the exemptStrategies inner loop is self-grief only.

findings.function: setTokenConfig L280 (unbounded normalizedExchangeRate), setDiscountRate L324 (cap = 100%), and all onlyOwner registry/funding setters
findings.description: Signature match across all registry/config/funding setters. normalizedExchangeRate is UNBOUNDED (setTokenConfig L280-287) and discountRate may be set to 10000 bps = 100% (setDiscountRate L325) => claimer pays 0 and receives all yield. These are DESIGNED owner levers (permanent-depeg handling + claim incentive) and the owner is trusted for KNOWING actions (Law 3); the DB note + ledger C-01 already class owner-drain framings as Low/known-issue. Do NOT re-escalate owner-drain to High. The IN-SCOPE, reportable slice is the non-obvious owner FOOTGUNS surfaced separately in manualReview (decimal-config mispricing PARK-01, nudge-split brick PARK-03, phlimbo allowance brick PARK-04).
vulnerableWhenMatched: critical params (rate, discount, strategy set) controlled by single owner key
presentMitigations: decimals bound <=18, discount bound <=10000, nudgeSplit bound <=100
findings.routeTo: severity-classifier (keep as C-01 Low); footgun variants in manualReview
findings.note: Recorded for completeness. Per known issues #4/#5 and ledger C-01, owner-drain High framings are suppressed; the footguns (PARK-01/03/04) are the in-scope hazards.

manualReview.function: claim() — skim loop L464-492 (delivers underlying to claimer) PRECEDES payment pull L509-520
manualReview.description: Delivery-before-payment: skimSurplus sends each strategy's underlying to msg.sender (L484) BEFORE the rewardToken payment is pulled (L509) — a CEI deviation and a doc/impl mismatch (NatSpec L424-447 + interface say pay-then-skim; code skims-then-pays => ledger L-03). If any strategy underlying is ERC777, the transfer to the claimer fires the claimer's tokensReceived hook mid-loop. Reentry into claim() is blocked by nonReentrant (L447); all other state-mutating functions are onlyOwner, so the cross-function reentrancy surface appears empty. Atomicity holds (a later revert rolls back the skims). LOW confidence because the guard mitigates the classic vector; parked so the scanner can confirm (a) no exploitable cross-function reentry exists and (b) skims-then-pays cannot be abused via a malicious-but-registered strategy callback.
vulnerableWhenMatched: external value delivered before payment collected
presentMitigations: skim recipient is msg.sender (claimer-controlled, not arbitrary)
manualReview.routeTo: code-scanner (cross-function reentrancy + strategy-callback abuse); cross-ref ledger L-03 (doc/impl) and PARK-02

manualReview.function: claim() L501 (minRewardTokenSupplied is a FLOOR, not a ceiling)
manualReview.description: claim() is an economic swap but its only guard, minRewardTokenSupplied (L501), reverts when actualPayment is BELOW the value — i.e. it is a minimum-payment (proxy for minimum-yield-received) floor that protects the claimer from spending an NFT + gas for a trivial yield. There is NO ceiling on what the claimer PAYS. Under normal 1:1+discount economics the claimer always profits by discount*yield, so the missing ceiling is benign; BUT if rewardToken decimals/exchangeRate are misconfigured (PARK-01) or the snapshot estimate diverges upward (PARK-06), a claimer can be charged far more than calculateClaimAmount previewed, with no max-payment revert. LOW confidence (a guard exists, just one-directional). Parked for econ-scanner to decide whether a max-payment param is warranted.
vulnerableWhenMatched: preview can diverge upward from actual (PARK-06)
presentMitigations: minRewardTokenSupplied floor protects against trivial-yield claims
payment derived from actual skimmed yield (self-consistent under correct config)

manualReview.function: claim() nudge split L512-516; whole-yield discount capture L497
manualReview.description: The `nudge` signature collides with the BatchNFTMinter winner-take-all pot pattern, but the conditions DO NOT match: here `nudge` receives a PROPORTIONAL share (actualPayment * nudgeSplit / 100, L512) of each claim, the recipient is OWNER-set (not caller-chosen), and there is no full-balance/count gate — so the nudge param is a RED HERRING, not the vulnerable construct. The genuinely relevant lens from this pattern's note ('permissionless front-run of a legitimately-funded pot is a valid MEV finding') is the DISCOUNT: claim() is permissionless (NFT-gated) and the first caller captures discount*(total pending yield across ALL strategies) in one shot (L497). Accumulated yield is a growing pot; whoever claims first takes the entire discount on it — a front-run/MEV race (overlaps PARK-06). Parked so the econ-scanner adjudicates the MEV materiality and confirms the nudge split is not exploitable.
vulnerableWhenMatched: permissionless capture of accumulated-yield discount by first claimer (MEV)
notVulnerableObserved: nudge payout is proportional, not winner-take-all
pot (payment) pulled fresh from claimer, not a pre-funded balance read after a loop
manualReview.routeTo: econ-scanner (MEV on discount capture); confirm nudge split is a non-issue

manualReview.function: claim() L501 (<); canClaim L706 (i<count); _validateAndBurnNFT L533 (index>0); setTokenConfig L282 (decimals>18); setDiscountRate L325 (rate>10000); setNudgeSplit L397 (split>100)
manualReview.description: Reviewed all boundary checks. They appear INTENTIONAL and correct: minRewardTokenSupplied uses < so equal-to-min passes (L501); decimals==18, rate==10000 (100%), split==100 are all allowed by design (L282/L325/L397); canClaim's i=1..<count matches nextIndex 'next-to-assign' semantics (valid ids 1..nextIndex-1); index>0 reserves id 0. No off-by-one identified. Parked only so a reviewer can confirm nextIndex semantics against the OOS NFTMinter (if nextIndex is inclusive of the last id, canClaim would skip the highest NFT — a cosmetic bot-helper bug, not a claim-path issue).
vulnerableWhenMatched: canClaim i<count vs i<=count depends on OOS nextIndex semantics
presentMitigations: canClaim is a view bot-helper off the claim path

manualReview.function: _normalizeAmount fallback L591; _denormalizeAmount fallback L622; claim L498
manualReview.description: No exact DB pattern; closest family is DIVISION-PRECISION (decimal handling). Both _normalizeAmount (L591) and _denormalizeAmount (L622) treat an UNCONFIGURED token (decimals==0 && rate==0) as 18-dec / 1:1 passthrough. If the owner sets rewardToken to a 6-dec token (USDC) but forgets setTokenConfig(rewardToken,6,1e18), _denormalizeAmount returns the raw 18-dec amount => claimers are charged ~1e12x intended (or, symmetrically, an unconfigured 6-dec STRATEGY token under-counts yield by ~1e12). Pure NON-OBVIOUS owner footgun (Law 3 in-scope hazard) that silently breaks core value-conservation — no malicious owner needed. setRewardToken (L360) does not require/derive a token config. Routed to econ-scanner for impact + deployment-wiring check.
vulnerableWhenMatched: rewardToken or a strategyToken left unconfigured while not actually 18-dec
manualReview.routeTo: econ-scanner + spec-conformance (deployment wiring guarantees); profile PARK-01

manualReview.description: No exact DB pattern (focus-family 'allowance-depletion bricking'). phlimbo PULLS its share via collectReward => transferFrom against a standing allowance the owner sets in approvePhlimbo (L369). The contract never tops up its own allowance, so once the allowance is exhausted EVERY claim reverts until the owner re-approves (ledger L-02 / PARK-04). Inverted-control design. Confirm L-02 still live at this commit and whether nudgeSplit reduces the per-claim pull (it does: phlimboAmount = actualPayment - nudgeAmount, L513).
manualReview.routeTo: code-scanner / interaction (phlimbo collectReward semantics); ledger L-02

manualReview.patternName: nudgeSplit>0 with unset nudge bricks all claims
manualReview.function: claim() L506 NudgeNotConfigured; setNudgeSplit L396 (no nudge!=0 guard)
manualReview.description: No exact DB pattern. setNudgeSplit (L396) does not require nudge != address(0). If the owner sets nudgeSplit>0 while nudge is unset, EVERY claim with yield reverts NudgeNotConfigured (L506, after the skim loop so still atomic). The permissionless claim path is fully bricked until the owner sets nudge or zeroes the split — a NON-OBVIOUS ordering footgun (Law 3 in-scope hazard). Recoverable by owner. Profile PARK-03.

manualReview.function: _validateAndBurnNFT L531-540 (burn at L536, before the skim loop)
manualReview.description: No exact DB pattern (focus-family 'ERC1155 burn accounting'). The NFT is burned (external INFTMinter.burn, L536) BEFORE the skim loop. Checked: exactly 1 unit at nftIndex is burned per successful claim; balanceOf>0 check precedes burn; a later revert (ZeroAmount / NudgeNotConfigured / InsufficientYield / strategy revert) rolls the burn back atomically (NFT-COST invariant). No double-burn, no burn-on-zero-yield (ZeroAmount reverts after the loop and rolls back). Reviewed as sound; parked only to confirm the OOS NFTMinter.burn has no receive hook / reentrancy (guarded by nonReentrant regardless) and that index>0 maps to a real dispatcher config.
